clips.text_zh: 聽日中期選舉結果一出，市場會點反應？有冇人落注？我估如果係紅區勝出，市場會 pump 得好癫；如果藍區贏，就係要跌轉深。香港咁窄，走勢一出真係好難止蝕。CFD 倉又爆多幾個就慘。呢個可能係今日最重要嘅 macro bet，唔係亂炒。
clips.text_en_b1: Impact of the midterm results tomorrow on financial markets. Any bets? I think that if the results are red, we pump like crazy. If they are blue, we take a fucked-up dive. The market will move sharply either way, so this is the important macro bet right now.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ thread asking how tomorrow's midterm results may move financial markets.

signal.rationale: The post gives a conditional election-market view but no clear entry, target, or stop.

clips.text_en_b2: How will financial markets react when tomorrow’s midterm results come in? I’m placing my bets: if the red states win, the market could pump like crazy, whereas a blue victory might send it into a deep dive. Because Hong Kong’s trading range is so narrow, any breakout will be difficult to stop or cut losses quickly, especially if several CFD positions get blown. This may be the most important macro bet today, not just random speculation.
clips.text_en_c1: How will tomorrow’s midterm results affect financial markets, and is anyone placing a bet on the outcome? My guess is that a Republican sweep would send markets into a euphoric rally, whereas a Democratic win could trigger a sharp sell-off. Hong Kong’s relatively narrow trading range may not offer much room to manoeuvre once the result emerges, and anyone holding leveraged CFD positions could be forced into liquidation. This may be the most consequential macro trade of the day rather than some random speculative move, although the direction is hardly certain.
clips.text_en_c2: How will financial markets react once tomorrow’s midterm results are confirmed? I’m placing my bets accordingly. If the Republicans sweep the key states, I expect a frenzied rally; should the Democrats prevail, the tape could crater without warning. Hong Kong’s market is narrow enough that any meaningful break will leave stop-loss orders scrambling for cover, and those fortunate enough to avoid a leveraged CFD liquidation may still count themselves lucky. Whatever the outcome, this is unquestionably the day’s most consequential macro wager, not merely a bout of speculative froth.

clips.text_zh: WTF 点解今日乜嘢都升，偏偏 SpaceX 同 Tesla 唔升？Elon 之前成日講會帶我發財，𠮶陣我更加以為 IPO 都係穩陣。依家就係 under the IPO，冇計個 prop firm 帳戶今日又畀人刮走一層皮。Tesla delivery、盈利同 Starship 消息一齊出，應驗期真係難頂。唔係唔信 Elon，係估值太撐。
clips.text_en_b1: WTF, why is everything up today except SpaceX and Tesla? Elon was going to make me rich. Now I am under the IPO. Tesla delivery numbers, earnings, and SpaceX launch news can all move the stock. I still believe in the company, but this valuation is difficult.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post complaining that SpaceX and Tesla fell while other assets rose.

signal.rationale: The post expresses a bearish view on Tesla and SpaceX relative to the rest of the market.

clips.text_en_b2: WTF, why is absolutely everything rising today except SpaceX and Tesla? Elon spent years promising he’d make me rich, so I assumed an IPO would be a safe bet. Now I’m under water on the IPO, and the prop firm account has been skinned alive again today. Tesla delivery figures, earnings, and Starship news can all affect the stock, but surviving that waiting period is brutal. I’m not anti-Elon; the valuation is simply too stretched.
clips.text_en_c1: Seriously, why is everything rising today except SpaceX and Tesla? Musk had spent so long promising to make me rich that I had assumed an IPO was practically risk-free. Now I’m sitting below the IPO price, and that’s before the prop firm account has been stripped of another layer. Tesla’s delivery figures, earnings, and news about Starship launches could all influence the stock, so waiting for the confirmation period is genuinely uncomfortable. I’m not abandoning my belief in the company; the problem is that its valuation has become increasingly difficult to justify.
clips.text_en_c2: For crying out loud, why is everything rising today except SpaceX and Tesla? Musk spent years promising to make me rich, and I had convinced myself that even the IPO was a sure thing. Now I’m sitting below the offering price, while my proprietary trading account has been skinned alive once more. Tesla’s delivery figures and earnings are landing alongside fresh Starship headlines, which makes the waiting period distinctly uncomfortable. I’m not abandoning the company, to be clear; I simply think the valuation has been stretched to breaking point.

clips.text_zh: Electrical engineer here. Been working for 11 years. I design products that work, and I love what I do. Yet I keep getting laid off or fired for silly reasons. Last time, it was a spelling error after I was put on a PIP. My managers told me to charge different hours, but coordinating them did not work. I was still blamed. I put myself through college because my parents refused to sign...
clips.text_en_b1: Electrical engineer here. I have worked for 11 years and I design products that work. I love my job, but I keep getting laid off or fired for silly reasons. Last time, it was a spelling error after I was put on a PIP. Multiple superiors told me to charge different hours, but coordinating them did not work, so I was still blamed.
clips.source_hint: An experienced engineer describes repeated layoffs and blame over billing hours and a minor spelling error.

signal.rationale: This is an engineering career post, not a trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: Electrical engineer here, with 11 years of experience designing products that actually work. I love my job, yet I keep getting laid off or fired for ridiculous reasons. Last time, it was a spelling mistake after I was placed on a PIP. Several managers told me to charge different hours, but coordinating those instructions did not work, and I was still blamed. I put myself through college because my parents refused to sign the necessary paperwork, although that is only part of the story.
clips.text_en_c1: I’m an electrical engineer with 11 years of experience, and I design products that actually work. I love my profession, yet I’ve repeatedly been laid off or fired for reasons that seem absurd. On the most recent occasion, a single spelling error led to my dismissal after I was placed on a performance improvement plan. Several managers instructed me to charge my time to different cost codes, but coordinating those assignments never worked properly, so I was blamed regardless. I put myself through college because my parents refused to sign anything, which makes these decisions particularly frustrating.
clips.text_en_c2: I’m an electrical engineer with eleven years of experience, designing products that genuinely work, and I love every minute of it. Nevertheless, I have been laid off or fired repeatedly, often for reasons that border on the absurd. On my last departure, the stated offence was a spelling error committed after I had been placed on a performance improvement plan. Several managers instructed me to charge different hours to different projects, but coordinating those instructions proved impossible, so I bore the blame regardless. I had put myself through college because my parents refused to sign the relevant paperwork.

clips.text_zh: Do you have a solid plan after LLMs replace you? Farming? Trades? 靠 AI 續命啦，連 GI report 都可能自動生成。不過 slope investigation、site supervision 同 contractor 溝通，唔係淨係識做計算就得。Automated drafting 可能快，但落去個 site 要 check 個 load path、問清楚 contractor 點做，最後仲係要有人頂住。個 plan 可能係 upgrade 自己，唔係轉去 farming。
clips.text_en_b1: Do you have a solid plan after LLMs replace you? Farming? Trades? Even civil engineering reports may become automated, but site supervision and contractor communication still need engineers. Someone must check the load path and make safe decisions on site.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread asks people what they will do if large language models replace their jobs.

signal.rationale: The post asks about career planning after AI replacement and gives no trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: Do you have a solid plan once LLMs replace you? Farming? Skilled trades? Relying on AI to keep civil engineering alive might work because even GI reports can now be generated automatically. However, slope investigation, site supervision, and contractor communication cannot be reduced to calculations alone. Automated drafting may be faster, but somebody still has to check the load path, clarify how the contractor intends to proceed, and make the final call on site.
clips.text_en_c1: Do you have a solid plan for life after large language models replace you? Will you take up farming, trades, or something else entirely? AI may already be capable of producing routine civil-engineering reports, but automated drafting is only the beginning. Slope investigations, site supervision, and communication with contractors still require professional judgement, because someone has to verify the load path, clarify how the work will be carried out, and stand behind the final decision. The practical response may therefore be to upgrade your own skills rather than retreat to farming, especially if your value lies on site rather than behind a desk.
clips.text_en_c2: Do you have a credible plan for the day large language models render you redundant? Would you farm? Take up a trade? Lean on AI to keep the lights burning, since even a GI report can now be generated automatically. Yet slope investigation, site supervision, and the endless negotiations with contractors cannot be reduced to producing calculations on demand. Automated drafting may well be faster, but somebody still has to verify the load path on site, interrogate the contractor’s methodology, and stand behind the final decision. The sensible plan is probably to upgrade your own capabilities, not retreat to farming.

clips.text_zh: BREAKING：Elon 喺中期選舉後出咗聲。個 post 話「America truly is dead」，又話「America」自己投咗票，仲希望情況再差啲。香港人成日話想返美國，但連 Elon 都咁講，會唔會真係應該諗下走？不過返 Florida 都要錢，100K USD 未儲到之前，考牌同人工更加唔可以停。
clips.text_en_b1: BREAKING: Elon Musk breaks his silence on the aftermath of the Midterms. America truly is dead, and America voted for it. The poster says he hopes it gets worse. Meanwhile, many Hong Kong people talk about returning to America.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ post reacts to Elon Musk's comments after the midterm election results.

signal.rationale: This is commentary about US politics and Elon Musk, with no actionable market setup.

clips.text_en_b2: BREAKING: Elon Musk has finally spoken about the aftermath of the Midterms. The post claims that “America truly is dead” and that America voted for this outcome; it also says he hopes the situation gets even worse. Many Hong Kongers regularly talk about returning to America, so does his statement mean we should seriously consider leaving? Although moving to Florida still costs money, before I’ve saved 100K USD, I cannot stop preparing for the exam or keep my income running.
clips.text_en_c1: BREAKING: Elon Musk has finally commented on the aftermath of the US midterms. According to the post, “America truly is dead,” while America itself voted for its condition and apparently hopes it gets even worse. Many Hong Kong residents regularly talk about returning to America, but if someone as prominent as Musk says this, should they start considering the option more seriously? That said, moving to Florida still costs money, and until I have saved USD 100,000, I cannot afford to stop studying for the relevant exams or weaken my earnings prospects. The ideal move may have to wait.
clips.text_en_c2: BREAKING: Elon Musk has finally spoken about the aftermath of the American midterms. According to the post, “America truly is dead,” and America voted for its own demise; worse still, Musk apparently hopes the situation deteriorates further. Hong Kongers have long talked about packing up and returning to the United States, but if even Musk sounds that hopeless, perhaps we should reconsider. That said, Florida remains expensive, and until I have saved the requisite 100,000 dollars, there is no option but to keep grinding through the examinations and the endless paperwork.

clips.text_zh: Whitepill Thread：熱朱古力先係最正嘅 pre-workout。任何人都可以開始 lifting，唔需要以前做過運動。你可以 escape skinnyfat mode，six months 內做到。有人用一年左右就會留意到你開始 lift。Beginner programming 好簡單，咩都 work。Diet 都一樣：食夠 protein，少食 fast food、candy 同 soda。唔使 gym subscription，都可以有唔錯嘅 physique。
clips.text_en_b1: Whitepill thread: hot cocoa is the best pre-workout edition. Anyone can start lifting, and you do not need previous sports experience. You can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. Beginner programming is easy. Eat enough protein and avoid fast food, candy, and soda. You do not need a gym membership.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ beginner whitepill thread explains simple lifting, diet, and physique expectations.

signal.rationale: This is fitness advice for beginners, not a trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: Whitepill thread: hot cocoa is the ultimate pre-workout. Anyone can start lifting, and you don’t need any previous sports experience. You can escape skinnyfat mode within six months, although some people need roughly a year before others notice that you have started lifting. Beginner programming is straightforward, and almost anything works to begin with. Diet follows the same simple rule: get enough protein and cut back on fast food, candy, and soda. You can build a decent physique without paying for a gym membership.
clips.text_en_c1: Whitepill thread: hot cocoa is the ultimate pre-workout. Anyone can begin lifting; you do not need a background in sport or any prior training experience. With consistent effort, you can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months, and after roughly a year, other people may start noticing that you lift. Beginner programming is straightforward, and almost any sensible routine will work. Diet follows the same uncomplicated logic: eat enough protein, while reducing your intake of fast food, candy, and soda. A gym membership is helpful, but it is not essential if you are willing to train consistently.
clips.text_en_c2: Whitepill thread: hot cocoa is unquestionably the finest pre-workout ritual. Anybody can begin lifting, and no prior athletic experience is required to get started. You can realistically escape skinnyfat mode in under six months, provided you remain consistent; indeed, some people go an entire year before their acquaintances begin noticing the transformation. Beginner programming is refreshingly straightforward, and the nutritional rules are no less forgiving: eat sufficient protein, while keeping fast food, candy, and soda firmly in the rear-view mirror. A gym membership is helpful, but it is by no means an entry fee.

clips.text_zh: Have there been fewer reverse traps appearing in manga and anime as time goes by? 以前成日見到，讀者以為係女主角，最後反轉變成男主或者路人。有時嗰個角根本唔係主角，只係被作者用嚟推剧情。依家好似冇咁多離套路，唔知係作者驚被罵，定係真係冇靈感。動漫文化都係一個 trend，唔代表每套都值得睇。
clips.text_en_b1: Have there been fewer reverse traps appearing in manga and anime as time goes by? Earlier stories often made readers think a heroine was the main character, then reversed it. Now the pattern seems less common. It may be a trend, but not every new series is worth reading.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ thread asks whether manga and anime contain fewer reverse traps over time.

signal.rationale: This is a discussion about manga storytelling, not a trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: Have manga and anime featured fewer reverse traps as time has gone by? Earlier stories frequently encouraged readers to assume that a heroine was the protagonist, only to reveal that she was actually the male lead or a nobody used to push the plot forward. Sometimes that character was not a central figure at all. Now the device seems less common, whether because authors fear criticism or because they have genuinely run out of ideas.
clips.text_en_c1: Have manga and anime gradually become less reliant on reverse traps? Earlier, readers were often led to believe that a heroine was the central protagonist, only for the story to reveal that she was actually the male lead or merely a minor character used to propel the plot forward. Sometimes the supposed heroine was not even the main character at all. The device now seems less common, although it is unclear whether creators fear criticism or have simply run out of inspiration. Like any broader trend within anime culture, this does not mean every new series is worth watching, and declining conventions do not automatically indicate a decline in quality.
clips.text_en_c2: Has anyone else noticed that reverse traps have grown rarer in manga and anime? Older series frequently misled readers into assuming a heroine was the central protagonist, only to reveal that the supposedly peripheral character was the true lead, or to consign the heroine to an anonymous supporting role. These days the convention seems less prevalent, whether because creators fear backlash or because they have genuinely run out of inspiration. Cultural trends shift, naturally, and the declining frequency of a particular device does not imply that every new series deserves your attention.
